A California Apple user has filed a class action lawsuit in court, accusing the company of misleading customers about the privacy protections of its "Hide My Email" feature. The details are as follows.

Apple sued over alleged 'Hide My Email' flaw

Recently, 404 Media reported that Apple had been aware of a so-called vulnerability for over a year that could expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple's "Hide My Email" feature allows users to create unique, randomly generated email addresses that forward messages to their personal inbox, so they don't have to disclose their real address when signing up for apps, websites, and newsletters.

This feature is available for free through "Sign in with Apple"; a more comprehensive version, included with the iCloud+ plan (starting at $0.99 per month), lets users create aliases for websites, newsletters, and other services.

According to 404 Media, a security researcher notified Apple of the vulnerability in June 2025, which could expose the real email address behind a "Hide My Email" alias.

Apple confirmed receipt of the report about a month later, but allegedly failed to fix the issue. In March 2026, the company said it had patched the vulnerability, but the researcher found it could still be exploited.

The following is excerpted from 404 Media:

Speaking of the lawsuit (reported by MacRumors), plaintiff Anthony Alvarez said:

Apple has been aware of the issue for over a year and still has not fixed the flaw—yet Apple continues to profit from "Hide My Email" and its privacy promises. The plaintiff is one of millions of customers who pay Apple for iCloud+ and rely on Apple's claim that "Hide My Email" protects their personal email addresses from being exposed. Plaintiffs and class members pay Apple for privacy—iCloud+ subscribers through a premium in the iCloud+ subscription fee, and all Apple customers through a premium in the price of Apple products, because Apple markets its products as equipped with enhanced privacy protections and features including "Hide My Email".

The lawsuit also claims this is not an isolated incident, citing a 2023 report that Apple's MAC address randomization feature could expose users' real hardware identification codes.

The lawsuit also alleges that the total amount sought by the proposed class members exceeds $5 million (excluding interest and costs), but does not explain how that figure was calculated.

Alvarez filed the lawsuit on behalf of himself and other Apple customers he claims were similarly affected. He is asking the court to certify the case as a class action, covering four proposed user groups:

  • A nationwide group of Apple customers who purchased devices and used "Hide My Email";
  • A California subset of the above users;
  • A nationwide group of iCloud+ subscribers who have used the feature;
  • A California subset of iCloud+ subscribers.

He is demanding a jury trial and, in addition to monetary damages in an amount to be determined, is asking the court to order Apple to fix "Hide My Email" or clearly disclose its limitations.

Apple has not yet responded to the lawsuit.

Do you think this class action should be certified? Let us know in the comments.
